I've worked this land for 40 years. My father farmed it before me. I know what this soil needs and what it doesn't.

My 10.1 mu runs wheat-maize rotation — wheat goes in the ground in October, comes off in June, then I plant maize right after on the same land. All 10.1 mu does both crops.

**Wheat:** I stopped using traditional seeds years ago. The improved varieties from the county extension — something like Jimai or Shannong — yield much better. I'll apply compound fertilizer before sowing and topdress urea at jointing, same as always. I do 4 irrigations: bottom water before sowing, then at jointing, heading, and grain fill. The well handles it fine. I'll spray herbicide in winter after emergence, then once more in spring for aphids and rust. Rotary till after maize harvest to work the stubble in.

**Maize:** Always hybrid, always. I've used Zhengdan 958 for years, reliable. After wheat harvest I plant directly — no reason to plough again, wastes moisture and time. I side-dress nitrogen at the big bell stage. Summer gets rain here so I only irrigate twice — once at planting if it's dry, once at silking if needed. Spray for corn borer once, herbicide once early.

Two people in the house, 10 mu — that's manageable. Not looking to change what works.
